items.description: A major city in the Chubut Valley founded by Welsh settlers, known for its paleontological museum and commercial importance.
facts: Home to the MEF Paleontological Museum
Founded as a railhead for the Central Chubut Railway
Key hub for the region's textile industry

items.description: A popular coastal city on the Golfo Nuevo, famous as a gateway to Peninsula Valdés for whale watching and wildlife tourism.
facts: One of the world's best spots for Southern Right Whale watching
Founded by Welsh immigrants in 1865
Major center for scuba diving and marine activities

items.description: A picturesque town in the foothills of the Andes, serving as a base for exploring the Los Alerces National Park and skiing.
facts: Home to the historic 'La Trochita' steam train
Gateway to the UNESCO-listed Los Alerces National Park
Popular winter sports destination at La Hoya

items.description: Argentina's second-largest city, Córdoba is a vibrant cultural hub known for its colonial history, universities, and surrounding hills.
facts: Home to the oldest university in Argentina
Features the UNESCO-listed Jesuit Block
Known for its lively 'cuarteto' music and nightlife

items.description: An important commercial and agricultural city in the south of Córdoba Province, often referred to as the 'Empire of the South'.
facts: Major center for corn and soy production
Home to the National University of Río Cuarto
Strategic transport hub in central Argentina

items.description: A modern and thriving city in central Córdoba, known for its dairy industry and the popular Festival of Festivals.
facts: Hosts the massive National Festival of Peñas
One of the most important dairy basins in the country
Located along the vital CTalamochita River

items.description: A premier tourist destination on the shores of Lake San Roque, famous for its summer theater and scenic mountain landscapes.
facts: Famous for its iconic Cuckoo Clock monument
Major hub for summer theater and entertainment
Gateway to the beautiful Punilla Valley

items.description: A productive city on the border between Córdoba and Santa Fe, known for its diverse industries and agricultural strength.
facts: Founded as an agricultural colony in 1886
Key center for metalworking and food industries
Located on a major national highway crossroads

items.description: The capital of Corrientes Province, located on the banks of the Paraná River and known for its colonial charm and carnivals.
facts: One of the oldest cities in Argentina
Famous for its elaborate and colorful carnival celebrations
Features a scenic waterfront 'costanera' walkway

items.description: The second-largest city in Corrientes, Goya is a river port famous for its tobacco industry and sport fishing.
facts: Hosts the prestigious Surubí National Festival
Major center for the tobacco processing industry
Founded in the late 18th century as a river port

items.description: A strategic border city on the Uruguay River, connected by an international bridge to the Brazilian city of Uruguaiana.
facts: Major international trade hub with Brazil
Birthplace of President Arturo Frondizi
Home to the oldest carnival in Argentina

items.description: A historic city in southern Corrientes, founded by Manuel Belgrano and known as the 'Cradle of the Chamamé'.
facts: First city founded by a native Argentine government
Important center for the regional cattle industry
Strong traditions in Chamamé folk music

items.description: The capital of Entre Ríos Province, Paraná is a scenic city perched on high cliffs overlooking the majestic Paraná River.
facts: Served as the capital of the Argentine Confederation
Known for its beautiful Urquiza Park
Connected to Santa Fe via an underwater tunnel

items.description: A thriving city on the Uruguay River, known for its citrus production, thermal springs, and the nearby Salto Grande dam.
facts: Major center for orange and lemon exports
Home to popular thermal water resorts
Strategic point for hydroelectric power generation

items.description: Located in southeastern Entre Ríos, Gualeguaychú is world-famous for hosting the largest and most spectacular carnival in Argentina.
facts: Home to the massive 'Carnival of the Country'
Popular river beach and camping destination
Known for its environmental activism and parks
